settled.about: who meets the guide and what they do
settled.decided: A colleague from accounting, alone at their Linux laptop with python3, LibreOffice Calc, a CUPS printer, and the invoicer folder on it: they save the client's lines, run the command with the client's rate, check the invoice on screen, and send it to lp.

settled.about: the command that shows the check met
settled.decided: On a fresh copy of the folder (git archive of HEAD plus the command's new modules) at ~/invoicer's place, and a sheet built as Calc saves the guide's example (Consulting 120 x 3, Travel 45.25 with an empty quantity), the guide's commands ran in order: the invoice matched the guide's block byte for byte and the totals counted by hand (360 + 45.25 = 405.25, 19 % = 76.9975 to 77.00, total 482.25); the quoted name with a space gave the same invoice; 0.19 gave a refusal naming the fix. The pipe to lp carries what the terminal shows, as test_i_print pins; all 86 tests pass. No lp was installed here, so the printer itself was not reached.

The guide starts from the invoicer folder on the laptop, as the check starts from a fresh copy of the folder; it names ~/invoicer and tells the colleague to use the folder's own place where it lies elsewhere. Nothing is installed, by P3.
The guide quotes the name only, after the ~/ part, since a quoted ~ is not expanded; an unquoted name with a space would get the usage refusal, which names no fix in the sheet.
One small sheet and its invoice, with amounts the colleague can count by hand, so they see the layout the command takes and what a right invoice looks like before checking their own.
